questions.enonce_markdown:
Bring out five (5) importance of  food and nutrition.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Five reasons why food and nutrition are important (1 mark each):

1. **Food supplies the energy** needed for work, play, movement and all the activities of the body.
2. **Food is needed for growth and development** of the body, especially in babies, children and adolescents.
3. **Food repairs and replaces** worn-out and damaged body cells and tissues.
4. **Food protects the body against disease**, because a well-fed body resists infection better, and a good diet prevents deficiency diseases such as rickets, anaemia and kwashiorkor.
5. **Food regulates the body processes**, for example digestion, body temperature and the working of the nerves, and so keeps the person healthy and active.

(Other correct points: a balanced diet makes it possible to plan meals within a budget; good nutrition improves the ability to learn and to work.)
themes: nutrients and their functions in food

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain the steps involved in cake making using the creaming method.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **creaming method** is used for rich cakes such as the Victoria sandwich or the Madeira cake. The steps are:

1. **Prepare.** Weigh the ingredients accurately, make sure the fat is soft (at room temperature), grease and line the cake tin, and heat the oven.
2. **Cream the fat and sugar.** Beat them together with a wooden spoon or a mixer until the mixture is pale, light and fluffy. This traps the air that will make the cake rise.
3. **Add the beaten eggs gradually.** Beat well after each addition. If the mixture starts to curdle (separate), add a spoonful of the flour.
4. **Fold in the flour.** Sift the flour with the baking powder (and salt), then fold it in gently with a metal spoon so that the air is not lost. Add a little milk if needed, to obtain a soft dropping consistency.
5. **Bake and cool.** Put the mixture into the prepared tin, level the top and bake in a moderate oven until the cake is risen and golden and a skewer pushed into the centre comes out clean. Leave it a few minutes in the tin, then turn it out on a wire rack to cool.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give five (5) reasons why some people are vegetarians.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Five reasons why some people are vegetarians (1 mark each):

1. **Religious or traditional beliefs** - some religions forbid or discourage the eating of meat (for example some Hindus, Buddhists and Seventh-day Adventists).
2. **Moral reasons** - they believe it is wrong to kill animals for food (animal welfare).
3. **Health reasons** - they believe that a diet rich in vegetables, fruit, cereals and pulses, and low in animal fat, is healthier.
4. **Economic reasons** - meat and fish are more expensive than cereals, beans and vegetables.
5. **Personal taste** - some people simply do not like the taste, smell or texture of meat.

(Other correct points: concern for the environment; family habits; the unavailability of meat in some places.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
i) State five (5) reasons for the increase in the number of cases of food poisoning.

(5 marks)

ii) List five (5) hygiene rules food handlers must follow to keep food safe.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Five reasons for the increase in the number of cases of food poisoning (1 mark each)**

1. **Poor personal hygiene of food handlers** - dirty hands, nails and clothes, or handling food while ill, pass germs to food.
2. **Poor storage of food** - cooked food left for hours in a warm place, and no refrigerator, allows germs to multiply quickly.
3. **Undercooked or badly reheated food** - germs survive when the food is not cooked or reheated thoroughly (for example poultry that is not cooked through).
4. **Cross-contamination** - raw meat, fish or eggs touch cooked food, or the same knife or board is used for both.
5. **Dirty kitchens, water and utensils, and flies and pests** - they carry germs to food; food prepared and sold in dirty surroundings or from unsafe water is also a danger.

(Other correct reasons: eating food after its expiry date; lack of training of food handlers; more people eating food prepared in large quantities or sold in the street.)

**(ii) Five hygiene rules that food handlers must follow (1 mark each)**

1. **Wash the hands thoroughly with soap and water** before handling food, after using the toilet and after touching raw meat or waste.
2. **Wear clean protective clothing** (an apron), and cover or tie up the hair.
3. **Keep the nails short and clean, and cover cuts and sores** with a waterproof dressing.
4. **Do not cough, sneeze, smoke or touch the face, hair or nose over food**, and do not handle food when suffering from diarrhoea, vomiting or an infection.
5. **Use clean utensils and separate boards and knives for raw and cooked food**, and keep food covered and at a safe temperature.
